content_html:
Monthly home maintenance should be brief and designed to catch problems before they become major repairs. A useful round covers water, heating and cooling, alarms, moisture, and frequently used equipment. It does not mean replacing filters or batteries every month; it means inspecting and acting based on condition, manufacturer schedule, and season.

Look for new leaks and moisture

Check under sinks, around toilets, the water heater, washer, and basement areas. A new stain, swollen material, or meter movement with no water use deserves investigation before damage spreads.

Inspect filters and airflow paths

Check the heating or air-conditioning filter and clean accessible grilles without opening equipment. Replace the filter when dirty or at the manufacturer interval rather than simply because the calendar month changed.

Test safety devices according to their instructions

Use the test button on smoke and carbon monoxide alarms as often as their manufacturer instructs and make sure extinguishers and flashlights are accessible. Replace expired units according to their actual service life.

Clean areas that accumulate lint and grease

Dryer lint screens, range hoods, dishwashers, and accessible drains benefit from regular checks. Buildup that returns unusually fast can indicate a ventilation, drainage, or use issue that needs correction rather than simply more cleaning.

faq.answer: Check the heating or air-conditioning filter and clean accessible grilles without opening equipment. Replace the filter when dirty or at the manufacturer interval rather than simply because the calendar month changed.

faq.question: Which safety devices should be checked regularly?
faq.answer: Use the test button on smoke and carbon monoxide alarms as often as their manufacturer instructs and make sure extinguishers and flashlights are accessible. Replace expired units according to their actual service life.
